out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: DOK Clean and Sanitize
violations.observation: There is no certified food manager on duty and the person in charge failed to explain the correct procedures for cleaning and sanitizing utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment. Observed the food, employee washing and rinsing equipment utensils, but not sanitizing them. There was no sanitizer located near the three compartment sink, indicating that sanitizing is not being routinely done.
violations.corrective_action: The person in charge shall know that all utensils and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be 1) washed with hot, soapy water to remove visible soil, 2) rinsed to remove residue, 3) sanitized using an approved sanitizer to reduce the number of bacteria and viruses and 4) air dried. Train all staff on the requirement to wash rinse and sanitize all equipment in utensils after use. Correct within 10 days.

out_items.name: Certified Food Protection Manager

violations.title: Food Manager Certificate & Responsibility
violations.observation: There is no Certified Food Manager present in the establishment.
violations.corrective_action: It shall be unlawful to operate a food establishment unless it is under the immediate control of a certified food manager. It is highly suggested that you have more than one employee with the food manager's license. ORS Interactive, Inc. (see handout provided) issues the required photo identification card with proof of successful completion of a certified food manager's exam. Failure to have a certified food manager on site during ALL hours of operation including food preparation, food service, and cleaning/sanitizing of equipment/utensils will result in closure of the establishment. It is recommended that more staff be certified as certified food managers in order to cover all operating hours and days when CFM is out, such as today. It’s not advisable to only have one person certified in an establishment. Correct with in 10 days.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: There was no one present to provide the EHS with the establishment employee health policy
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. The EHS left employee health policy documents with the person in charge. Complete the forms within three days.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. The EHS left the PIC a copy of the Fairfax County model policy, which will be implemented as the establishment policy

out_items.name: Hands clean and properly washed

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. Observe the food employee washing soiled equipment and utensils, then handle raw chicken, then put his bare hands in a pan of rice that was soaking in a bowl of water, all without washing hands.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. Train employees on when to properly wash hands within three days.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at each handwashing sink. There are several motorized paper towel dispensers in the establishment, none of which were working during the inspection, so paper towels were not available at those locations. This was a violation that was supposed to have been corrected before this inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. Repair the paper towel dispensers or provide paper towels at each hand washing sink in some other way. MANDI MEDITERRANEAN (Inspection Date: 03/24/2026) Page 3 of 6

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw ground beef was being stored over raw fish in the walk-in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. The raw fish was discarded due to the fact that it was previously frozen and still in the sealed package and also because it was out of temperature at 52° in the walk-in. The EHS will provide the PIC with a poster that shows how to properly store foods in the refrigerator. Ensure that staff properly store foods in the refrigerator to avoid cross-contamination of foods. MANDI MEDITERRANEAN (Inspection Date: 03/24/2026) Page 2 of 6

out_items.name: Food-contact surfaces cleaned and sanitized

violations.title: Food Contact Surface, Clean after Use
violations.observation: Equipment food-contact surfaces/utensils were not observed cleaned before any possible contamination. The large mixing bowl was not cleaned after its last use and was visibly soiled. The Ninja brand Mixer was not properly cleaned after its last use and was visibly soiled. The inside of the microwave in the kitchen was not cleaned after its last use and was visibly soiled. The inside of the grinder had metal shavings in it and was not cleaned after its last use.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned at any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred. Clean and sanitize all the equipment listed above as soon as possible or within 3 days.

violations.title: Before Use After Cleaning
violations.observation: Observed an employee washing and rinsing equipment and utensils at the three compartment sink without sanitizing them. The three compartment sink was not properly set up and there was no sanitizer present indicating that no equipment is being sanitized.
violations.corrective_action: All utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use and after cleaning. Train staff in the proper procedures for washing machine and sanitizing all equipment and utensils. Correct within three days.

out_items.name: Proper hot holding temperatures

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: rice and the rice cooker was 106°F. It was unclear if the food was being stored in this unit or being reheated in this unit.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. Hot food such rice must be held at 135°F. If the rice cooker is being used to reheat the rice after it’s already been cooked, it must be reheated to 165°F within two hours. Please ensure staff is following this procedure. The food employee said he would reheat the rice in the microwave. If so, the food must be covered and reheated to 165°F and left to sit covered for at least two minutes. Ensure staff is following this procedure.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: There were several cold holding violations observed during today’s inspection. In the walk-in refrigerator, which had an ambient temperature of 50º, cooked ground beef was 52°, cooked Gyro meat was 52°, cooked lamb/beef Gyro meat was 50°, another pan of cooked Gyro meat was 50°, raw ground beef kebabs were 49°, raw chicken was 50°, cooked tandoori chicken was 52°, cooked rice with chicken was 48°, a large pan of cooked rice was 57°, a smaller pan of cooked rice was 56°, a pan of baba ghanoush was 50°, a pan of cooked eggplant was 49°, cooked beef with grape leaves was 49°, cooked mixed roasted vegetables were 49°, and masala sauce was 58°. On the front buffet unit, eggplant stuffed grape leaves were 48° and 47° for more than 24 hours according to the employee. There were several foods being stored at room temperature in the kitchen including: cooked gyro meat was 60° for 20 minutes according to the employee; curry/Tikka masala sauce was 62° for 10 to 15 minutes according to the employee; tomato sauce was 54° for 10 to 15 minutes according to the employee, and marinating raw chicken was 58° for 10 to 15 minutes according to the employee. A can of whipped cream, which according to the label is required to be refrigerated, was being stored on the counter at room temperature in the storage area.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. All foods in the walk-in were discarded due to temperature abuse. The walk-in needs service and should not be used to store TCS foods until it is repaired. Since the establishment has limited refrigeration, these repairs should be the highest priority. Otherwise the establishment might be closed for lack of sufficient refrigeration. The grape leaves on the buffet were discarded due to temperature abuse. Regarding the food stored at room temperature in the kitchen, these foods were stored in the walk-in previously. The employee stated they were out of the walk-in for only 10 to 15 minutes, however, since they were stored in the walk-in which is not working properly, they were already out of temperature for an extended time. These foods are all discarded as well. The can of whipped cream was discarded.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food, Disposition
violations.observation: Observed the following ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food being held for more than the specified time/temperature allowed (7 days): the container of cooked lamb and beef Gyro stored in a walk-in refrigerator had a date mark of 3/15/26, which was 10 days ago. This exceeds the 7 days allowed for TCS RTE (ready to eat) food prepared on site to be held.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be discarded if it: 1) exceeds 7 days or at 41F (except the time it is frozen); or 2) is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day. The container of gyro meat was discarded. Train staff on date-marking requirements. Routinely check the refrigerator for RTE foods that are nearing or have exceeded their maximum holding time of 7 days.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: several foods prepared on site such as hummus, baba ghanoush, cooked rice, cooked Gyro meat, cooked ground beef, and others were not being properly date marked.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. Please ensure that foods are properly date marked and train staff on date marking requirements. Correct within 10 days.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Working containers of poisonous and toxic materials are not properly labeled with a common name. There was an unlabeled chemical spray bottle in the kitchen area.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. Ensure that all toxic chemicals are probably labeled at all times. Correct within 10 days.

out_items.name: Approved thawing methods used

violations.title: Proper Thawing Methods for ROP Fish
violations.observation: An ROP (vacuum-packed) package of previously frozen tilapia, which was thawed in the walk-in refrigerator was not cut open as required.
violations.corrective_action: The packaging of frozen vacuum-packed fish must be cut open when thawing to prevent growth of bacteria that grows in a reduced oxygen atmosphere. Since the fish was stored in the walk-in, which was not working properly, and 50°F, it was discarded.

out_items.name: Thermometers provided and accurate

violations.title: Air/Water Thermometers Accuracy, Only Degrees F
violations.observation: The ambient (air/water) temperature measuring device located in the following unit is not accurate in degrees F. The unit is scald in 10 degree increments.
violations.corrective_action: Ambient air and water temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to +/-3 degrees F in the intended range of use. Obtain a properly scaled thermometer in 10 days.

out_items.name: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

violations.title: Openings Protected from Pest Entry
violations.observation: There are gaps underneath the seals at the front door, the side door, and both garage doors which will allow pest to enter from the outside. This was an issue that was supposed to have been corrected prior to the first routine inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Fill or close holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings to protect against the entry of insects and rodents. Close these gaps to prevent pest entry. When repairs are completed, light should not be visible when looking at the gaps from inside.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. A case of camp potatoes were stored on the floor under the washing sink. Several foods were stored on the floor in the walk-in freezer.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. The food employee moved the case of potatoes during the inspection. Move all food stored on the freezer floor to suitable shelving within 10 days. Train employees to keep foods stored off the floor. MANDI MEDITERRANEAN (Inspection Date: 03/24/2026) Page 4 of 6

out_items.name: Personal cleanliness

violations.title: Hair Restraints
violations.observation: Employees observed working in the food service area without proper hair restraints.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wear hair restraints such as hats, visors, hair nets or beard nets to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service items. This section does not apply to food employees such as counter staff who ONLY serve beverages and wrapped or packaged foods, hostesses, and wait staff. All food staff, including dishwashers, are required to wear hair restraints. Correct as soon as possible or within 10 days.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items, Stored off Floor, Clean Location
violations.observation: Observed equipment, such as pots and single service items, such as take out containers stored on the floor in the establishment
violations.corrective_action: Cleaned equipment and utensils, laundered linens, and single-service items shall be stored in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches off the floor on NSF approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Discontinuous restoring equipment and utensils on the floor. Store on approved shelving. Correct as soon as possible or within 10 days.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: the ambient temperature of the walk-in refrigerator was 50º F and most foods in the unit were above 41ºF and between 48º and 58ºF.
violations.corrective_action: Since the establishment has limited refrigeration (there are only two small refrigerators in the establishment), this should be a priority issue and requires immediate attention. Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. Correct as soon as possible and notify your EHS when corrected.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Design/Construction
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surface of the following equipment is not designed or constructed to be easily cleanable: there is a wooden pallet under the mixer. One of the kitchen microwaves was stored on an unopened cardboard rice cooker box.
violations.corrective_action: Bare wood is not approved for use in a kitchen and the pallet is less than 6 inches off the floor and does not allow for proper cleaning of the floor. Remove the pallet. A cardboard box is not an approved material for shelving in a food establishment. Remove the cardboard box. Correct both violations within 10 days.

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following equipment is not operating properly and/or is in poor repair: the manual dicing machine located on the wall near three compartment sink was severely rusted and is no longer approved for use. The metal can opener was severely rusted and is no longer approved for use. These were issues that were supposed to have been corrected before the establishment opened or within 30 days of opening.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. Remove the dicer from the establishment and fill the holes in the walls left after removing to prevent pest entry.

out_items.name: Plumbing installed, proper backflow devices

violations.title: Backflow Prevention, Approved Device Provided
violations.observation: Observed the lack of an approved backflow prevention device on the water supply system. The splitter on the mop sink is not approved. This is an issue that was supposed to have been corrected prior to opening.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be installed to preclude backflow of a solid, liquid, or gas contaminant into the water supply system at each point of use at the food establishment, including on a hose bib if a hose is attached or on a hose bib if a hose is not attached and backflow prevention is required by Law by installing an approved backflow prevention device as specified under 5-202.14. Remove the splitter. If a splitter is needed, install a Hydro Systems 1951 Pressure Bleed Dual Valve.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: Observed the following components of the physical structure are not maintained: The ceiling panels in the food prep and kitchen area are badly stained. Several ceiling panels are missing or misplaced. The lighting fixtures in the food prep area are all four bulb fixtures, however, many of the bulbs are not working. One of the shelving units in the walk-in refrigerator is badly rusted. There’s a piece of broken coving underneath the soda machine in the dining area. There’s a piece of broken corner coving between the kitchen and the three compartment sink areas. These are all issues that were issued that were to be corrected prior to opening.
violations.corrective_action: Replace all stained ceiling panels and ensure all ceiling panels are in place with no openings visible. Ensure all light bulbs are working properly and all fixtures are working properly. Remove the rust or replace the rusted shelving. Repair the broken coving. Correct all issues listed as soon as possible or within 10 days.

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: Observed that the kitchen floor and walls were visibly soiled and not being cleaned frequently enough.
violations.corrective_action: Clean the floor as often as necessary to keep it clean. This should be done at least on a daily basis. More often as needed. Clean the floor and walls as soon as possible or within 10 days.

violations.title: Premises Free of Unnecessary Items/Equipment
violations.observation: Observed that items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment are being stored on the premises. Observed several pieces of excess/leftover equipment in the establishment and stored under the prep table next to the prep refrigerator. This is an issue that was supposed to be corrected prior to opening.
violations.corrective_action: Remove unnecessary items, including equipment which is no longer in use, from the premises to allow for regular and effective cleaning and to prevent harborage conditions. Remove all excess/leftover equipment. Correct within 10 days.

out_items.name: Adequate ventilation and lighting, designated areas used

violations.title: Protective Shielding on Light Bulbs
violations.observation: Observed at least one cracked light shield in the kitchen area. This was an issue that was to be corrected before the establishment opened for business or within 30 days of opening.
violations.corrective_action: Replace the cracked light shield as soon as possible or within 10 days.
